contributions.summary: Separates team performance, player development, and coach prestige before weighting.
Recognizes memory decay and Internet expansion as distinct cross-era mechanisms.
Keeps subjective AHP and objective GRA-MaxEnt branches separate until final fusion.
Introduces candidate-normalized grey-relation depth and dispersion as optimization constraints.
Uses a normalized product, acting as a joint-support gate rather than an arithmetic average.
Translates the model chain into a short public memo.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Division-aware winning percentage, stability/variance, and significant victories.
Awards, first overall draft picks, and APR discussion.
Coach awards and Google search exposure.
Equal-value assumptions and high-specificity first-pick proxy.
WRSP ratio and trend classes, followed by explicit fitting failure.
Career awards/available awards and championships/available championships.

dependency_graph.closure_status: The positive workflow is explicit through comprehensive weights, but the coach-score equation, source data, AHP matrices, timeline corrections, and valid sensitivity metric are missing.
edges: adjusted_value and hierarchy evidence enter AHP
adjusted_value forms raw evaluation matrix Y
ranking and weights enter sensitivity and transfer testing
feedbacks: Sensitivity and transfer results are intended to bound confidence in the final rankings, although the supplied tests are insufficient.

independent_extensions.summary: Audit threshold sensitivity and compare screened-out candidates before ranking.
Fit an explicit cohort/age-period model with centered time variables and out-of-sample checks.
Publish judgment matrices, expert protocol, eigenvectors, CI/RI/CR, and unrounded weights by sport.
Use benefit, cost, and target normalization separately; publish x0 and rho sensitivity.
Repair the feasible-set notation, prove nonempty compact feasibility, and publish solver diagnostics.
Publish candidate matrices, adjusted values, final score equation, scores, tie rules, and uncertainty.
Replace signed EI with mean absolute rank change, Spearman/Kendall, top-k overlap, and score elasticity.
Document target-domain feature mapping, re-estimated weights, scores, and external validation.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A stage-complete summary may improve traceability; award status does not prove judge preference.
A visible hierarchy may help reviewers inspect an abstract evaluation target.
Aligned weight tables permit independent arithmetic checks and reveal zero-weight tradeoffs.
A public-facing memo may improve audience fit when it mirrors the technical chain and retains caveats.

section_map.summary: Four paragraphs: metrics/proxies/filtering -> dual weights -> ranking -> sensitivity and transfer.
NCAA institutional hierarchy and top-division rationale.
Eligibility, proxy, equal-importance assumptions, and model symbols.
Team, player, and prestige dimensions with indicator-by-indicator rationale.
Division, win-rate, tenure, and scandal gates.
WRSP, trend typology, failed fitting route, and three verbal corrections.
Hierarchy and claimed subjective weight method.
Normalization, similarity, new GRDC intermediate, constrained entropy optimization.
Weight fusion, top-five rankings, and sport-specific weight tables.

limitations: All 22 physical PDF pages were rendered and visually reviewed; no blank or obviously clipped page was found.
PDF p1-p17 contains the paper, PDF p18-p20 references, and PDF p21-p22 a substantive author-written Magazine Article memo.

The path and filename deterministically classify the source as A, while the rendered cover says Problem Chosen B; plan.md forbids content-based reclassification, so the anomaly is preserved as provenance.
The coach-award normalization variable and equation are visibly absent in the source PDF, appearing as two commas; this is not an extraction-only defect.
Several formulas contain ambiguous notation, especially the scalar-to-interval subset symbol in the MaxEnt dispersion constraint.

deliverables: Define and justify a comprehensive set of coach-evaluation indicators.
Correct cross-era bias in awards, championships, and public-search exposure.
Separate AHP subjective weights from GRA-GRDC-MaxEnt objective weights and combine them.
Rank football, basketball, and baseball coaches and communicate the result to a public audience.
Test sensitivity to weight changes and demonstrate transfer to women volleyball.
task_reconstruction.reconstruction_limit: The operative task is clear from the paper, but its cover declares Problem B despite the path-only A label; this mismatch is not used to rewrite the manifest class.

title: Who is the Centennial Best Coach?
unresolved_questions: Why do the authoritative path and filename label A while the rendered cover declares Problem B?
What is the missing coach-award web-count normalization formula on PDF p8-p9?
What is the WRSP ratio direction and what final corrected search values were used?
What are the AHP judgment matrices, expert source, consistency statistics, and unrounded weights?
How are variance/stability and any target-type indicators directionally normalized?
What ideal sequence and distinguishing coefficient rho produce the reported GRA values?
What does the subset symbol in Eq.11 mean, and is the MaxEnt feasible set compact and nonempty?
What final score equation and candidate data produce the rankings?
How can the signed-rank EI be nonzero for a complete reranking of the same twenty candidates?
What data and benchmark support the women-volleyball universality claim?

verification.summary: Rounded rows approximately reproduce comprehensive weights under Eq.13.
Twenty-percent variance-weight change is evaluated with EI/SI, but the metric is invalid.
Women volleyball ranking demonstrates use without external validation.
Consistency with documents is asserted without a defined benchmark.

visualization_observations.summary: Cover visibly states Problem Chosen B while filename/path classify A; Summary gives the four-paragraph method-to-ranking route.
Knute Rockne Google Trends sketch supports the early-coach slow-decline trend category, not a calibrated correction.
Mike Krzyzewski Google Trends sketch supports a modern stable/peaked category but is paired with a false retirement statement.
AHP hierarchy maps the target to team performance, player performance, personal prestige, and seven final indicators.
Raw matrix, benefit-type normalization, and standardized matrix form the GRA input pipeline.
Grey relation coefficient and ideal-sequence differences expose the missing rho and ideal-sequence dependencies.
GRDC normalization and dispersion create data-dependent intermediates for weight bounds.
Weight range and dispersion constraints define the intended MaxEnt feasible region, including the ambiguous subset symbol.
Maximum-entropy objective and weight constraints define the objective-weight optimization.
Normalized elementwise product combines AHP and MaxEnt-GRDC weights and exposes zero-weight veto behavior.
Three side-by-side top-five rankings are the central decision output but omit coach scores and uncertainty.
Football AHP, MaxEnt-GRC, and comprehensive weights permit approximate Eq.13 reconciliation.
Basketball weights show personal honor dominance and zero draftee objective weight.
Baseball weights show personal honor is zeroed by multiplicative pooling.
Signed mean rank change is the sensitivity metric and is mathematically zero for any complete reranking of the same candidates.
Reported sensitivity indices 0.01% and 0.005% conflict with the EI identity and mix rank and percentage units.
Women volleyball top-five list demonstrates portability use but lacks target inputs, scores, weights, or benchmark.
Two-page public memo translates the technical workflow into indicators, temporal correction, dual weights, and a final ranking.

weaknesses.summary: Coach-award weighting cannot be reproduced or silently reconstructed.
Summary language about two proposed modification models overstates the implemented timeline model.
The example is factually false and directly affects the trend-category explanation.
The subjective weights are reported values rather than reproducible outputs.
The source may reward unstable coaches if raw variance is used.
Grey relation coefficients and objective weights are not unique from supplied evidence.
The feasible region is mathematically ambiguous and cannot be silently repaired.
A maximizer need not be attained on a nonclosed feasible set.
Rankings cannot be recomputed from the frozen paper.
Any two complete rankings are permutations of 1..20, so EI must be zero.
The test does not cover the full weight simplex or uncertainty in data.
No target input, mapping, scores, weights, or external benchmark supports universality.
Rounding is plausible, but unrounded values are required for exact replication.
The consensus-veto behavior is material to interpretation but not discussed.
The anomaly must remain visible in every frozen identity record and cannot be used to silently rewrite A-F class.

writing_logic.summary: metrics/proxies/filtering -> subjective/objective weights -> final ranking -> tests
subjective judgment gap -> objective need -> four-step response
data burden -> bounded proxies -> opportunity correction
bias mechanisms -> competing corrections -> failed fit -> reduced proxy role
subjective hierarchy || objective data relation -> separate weights
v and w -> normalized product z -> unstated score -> rankings
weight perturbation -> invalid rank metric; target transfer -> output-only demonstration
reader question -> ranked answer -> plain three-step method -> closing
